title: Courts go paperless as e-filing launched
byline: Electronic filing of Court cases has been introduced at the Colombo District Court as part of the island-wide e-Courts Project implemented under the Judicial Service Commission.

title: Solar sector at risk, Chamber of Commerce tells president
byline: The National Chamber of Commerce of Sri Lanka has urged President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to intervene urgently over policy concerns affecting the country’s rooftop solar energy sector, warning that the changes could undermine energy security and economic recovery.

title: Over 53,000 people with kidney disease receive Rs. 10,000 monthly allowance: Minister
byline: As many as 53,604 people suffering from kidney disease are currently receiving a monthly allowance of Rs. 10,000, Minister of Social Security Upali Pannilage told Parliament today.

title: Committee on High Posts approves Ambassador, High Commissioner appointments
byline: The Committee on High Posts of Parliament has approved the appointments of a new Ambassador, a High Commissioner and the Chairman of a state institution.

title: Weather impact to ease as depression weakens
byline: The impact of the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal on Sri Lanka’s weather is expected to gradually decrease from tomorrow (25) as the system weakens into a depression, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Avoid taking painkillers amid rising flu cases: Expert
byline: A surge in Influenza A H1N1 infections is currently being detected in Sri Lanka, with an increase in positive samples identified by the National Influenza Centre at the Medical Research Institute (MRI), Consultant Virologist Dr. Chrishan Jude Jayamaha said.

title: Italian woman falls to death
byline: A young italian woman who fell down the elevated region of the Rawanaella waterfall at a height of more than 100 feet yesterday afternoon died on admission to Demodara hospital.

title: After 22A, NPP Govt to begin work on new Constitution
byline: Despite the Government’s sudden move to enact the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, which provides for an increase in the retirement age of superior court judges, the introduction of a new Constitution, a key election promise of the ruling National People’s Power (NPP), will come under formal discussion within the party next year, an official said.

title: Showers forecast in several areas today
byline: The Meteorology Department has forecast showers at times in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces, as well as in the Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts today.

title: Regulation or control? NGO Bill puts civic space under scrutiny: TPA’s Barath
byline: The proposed NGO law could weaken organisations that help citizens challenge government decisions, defend their rights and obtain essential assistance, Democratic People’s Front Vice President for International Affairs and TPA Politburo Member Barath Arullsamy warned.

title: No move to curtail rooftop solar: Energy Minister
byline: The government has dismissed reports alleging that it is taking steps to curtail rooftop solar power while promoting other energy sources.

title: 64% of pre-schoolers get 30+ minutes of daily screen time in SL, raising concerns - Survey
byline: Excessive screen use among preschool children is raising concerns over their brain development, language and social skills, physical activity and overall health, with 64% of children spending more than 30 minutes a day on screens, according to a recent survey conducted by the Health Promotion Bureau in collaboration with the University of Colombo and UNICEF.

title: Counsellors warn of growing sexual withdrawal among married men
byline: Psychological counsellors have raised concerns about a growing pattern of sexual withdrawal among married men in Sri Lanka, saying a lack of intimacy is increasingly contributing to tension and conflict in relationships.

title: SJB mulls no-confidence motion against Speaker
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) is considering bringing a no-confidence motion against Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne, SJB General Secretary Ranjith Madduma Bandara said.

title: Northern Sea, Arabian Sea used as key drug smuggling routes to Sri Lanka
byline: Drug trafficking networks are using different maritime routes to smuggle various types of narcotics and other contraband into Sri Lanka, with the Northern Sea and Arabian Sea emerging as key routes for different categories of illicit cargo, according to the Sri Lanka Navy.

title: I only meant a ‘division in society’, Bimal says later in verbal clash with Dayasiri
byline: Later, during the debate, in a heated exchange of words with Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP Dayasiri Jayasekera, Leader of the House Bimal Rathnayake said he meant a division in society only.

title: Anti-rabies drive: 1.7 million dogs vaccinated last year
byline: Sri Lanka is stepping up efforts to prevent rabies by expanding dog vaccination, sterilisation and public awareness programmes, with nearly 1.7 million dogs vaccinated in 2025 as the country continues its push to reduce human deaths from the disease, according to the National Anti-Rabies Campaign of the Public Health Veterinary Services.

title: GCE O/L rescrutiny results released
byline: The Department of Examinations has released the rescrutiny results of the 2025 (2026) General Certificate of Education Ordinary Level (GCE O/L) Examination.

title: Only fractional division in government over 22A – Bimal admits
byline: For the first time, Leader of the House Bimal Rathnayake admitted in Parliament yesterday that, though the government has always maintained a unified approach, there was a fractional division over the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, but the opposition would not be able to exploit it to its advantage.

title: High waves, sea inundation warning issued for Southern coastal areas
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued a warning about high waves and possible seawater inundation in nearshorareas stretching from Beruwala to Matara via Galle.

title: Iran offers US deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days
byline: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says his country has proposed a deal to the US that would see the Strait of Hormuz reopened within a week.

title: Plane crash in DR Congo killes 14 including senior military officials
byline: At least 14 people, including senior military officials, were killed on Friday when a Congolese army plane crashed in the southwest of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

title: 22nd Amendment to the Constitution: Arguments for and against
byline: A central issue in the debate over Sri Lanka’s proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution has been the retirement age and tenure of Superior Court judges, with arguments focusing on judicial independence, the retention of experienced judges and the possible impact on delays in the administration of justice.

title: Police warn leasing firms over unlawful seizures
byline: The Sri Lanka Police have clarified the legal procedures governing the repossession of vehicles and equipment by leasing and finance companies, warning against forceful seizures and breaches of the peace.

title: 36-year-old dies following gas cylinder explosion at Polonnaruwa Kidney Hospital
byline: A 36-year-old man has died after sustaining injuries in a gas cylinder explosion at the kitchen of the Polonnaruwa National Nephrology Hospital, police said.

title: 44 kg of hashish, 13 kg of cocaine destined for Sri Lanka seized at Toronto Airport
byline: The Canada Border Services Agency has seized suitcases packed with illicit substances bound for Sri Lanka at Toronto Pearson International Airport earlier this month.
